quote_original: Then he will have fulfilled his purpose.
context_before: Listen carefully now to these words from Paul’s letter to the Philippians: -“Christ Jesus who – though he was in the form of God – thought it not robbery to be equal with God, emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, and was born in the likeness of men. And being found in human form he became obedient unto death, even death on the cross.-” Your body is the cross upon which Jesus Christ is crucified. And it is there he will remain until he transforms your lowly body into the one form with his glorious body.
context_after: I tell you: Jesus Christ has actually taken upon himself your body of humility and become its slave by feeding it, bathing it, clothing it, and caring for it in every way; yet Jesus Christ is not of this world. But in time he will completely transform you into his glorious body, for he is the redeemer, who – having assumed your body – will redeem it, thereby becoming the redeemed.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Vine (1969-04-04).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-04-04 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: When you imagine, God is acting.
context_before: Jesus Christ is God himself, who became you, individually. Your awareness is He.
context_after: He is the true vine and the vinedresser, for he is your imagination, imagining you. If you really understand this, you will start pruning your thoughts. If you don’t and continue to believe Jesus Christ is other than your Self, you will persist in allowing your wanton energy to run wild, to swell into irregular twigs, and bear unlovely things in your world.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Vine (1969-04-04).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-04-04 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: That is what you are called upon to do.
context_before: When you become aware of those in need, even though you do not know them personally, do you use your imagination to lift them from that state?
context_after: If you represent them to yourself as you would like them to be, and persuade yourself it is true, that branch will change in your world. You do not eliminate the state of need. It remains for anyone to be aware of, but you – having lifted yourself out of the state – see it no more.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Vine (1969-04-04).

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: Then you will say, from personal experience, -“I am he.-“
context_before: Prune your vine morning, noon, and night; and then — when you least expect it – a series of wonderful, supernatural experiences will be yours, as God reveals himself in you – not as another, but as your very Self.

quote_original: Then what a joy is ours!
context_before: Only one being returns. That being is God the Father, the sender, now one with his Son, the sent. Entering this world of many, we are the gods, sons of the Most High, yet one with our Father. When, as the son, we overcome death, we return with greater brilliance and translucency because of our victory over death.

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-04-04 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: And I wore it faithfully until the night of the transfiguration.
context_before: One night in 1946, I wore that body. It’s the same body I gave up when I took upon myself this body of a slave in order to redeem it. That night, while still aware of being Neville, I – the invisible – became a visible being by nailing myself upon this cross called Neville.
context_after: So I know the thrill that is in store for you when your body of slavery is transformed into a body of immortality. You see, the being you really are is Jesus Christ and cannot die. You who were before that the world was, came down into this world of death to overcome it, to rise as one being; for you – the redeemer – will know yourself to be one with the redeemed.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Vine (1969-04-04).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-04-04 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: So I, the Father, began to prune the vine.
context_before: When I first found this vine I could hardly sleep for days and days, I was so disillusioned thinking of the responsibility that was now on my shoulder – responsibility that I had always placed upon the shoulder of another. But once I accepted the fact that Jesus Christ is my human imagination and the cause of everything I am aware of, I knew I couldn’t pass the buck any more, but had to do something about it.
context_after: The entire 15th chapter of the Book of John is devoted to this pruning of the vine. He starts off: -“I am the true vine. My Father is the vinedresser.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The True Vine (1969-04-04).
